name: SmartUsername – Secure Admin Login Renamer & Username Editor Tool
author: Pritam Sonone

sections.description:
WordPress does not let you edit a username after an account is created. SmartUsername adds a screen under Users > Change Username that renames an existing account in place, so posts, comments, roles, passwords and user meta stay attached to the same user.

Features

  • Rename any user: pick the account from a list, or use the “Change username” link on the Users screen or next to the Username field on the profile screen.
  • Security check: warns on the Dashboard and Users screens when an account uses a username that login attacks guess first (admin, administrator, root, your site name and similar), with a one-click Rename button. The notice can be dismissed and only returns if something new is found.
  • Email the user: optionally send the renamed user a short email with the old and new username and the login link.
  • Self-service (optional, off by default): let chosen roles change their own username from Profile > Change Username, with a waiting period between changes.
  • WP-CLI: wp smartusername rename, wp smartusername check and wp smartusername log for agencies and scripts.
  • Live validation: as you type, the plugin checks length, allowed characters and whether the name is taken.
  • Same rules as WordPress core: at most 60 characters; letters, numbers, spaces and . – _ @ only; names blocked by the illegal_user_logins filter are refused.
  • Optional author slug update: also change the author URL slug (user_nicename). The old author URL redirects to the new one with a 301.
  • Safe sign out: renaming your own account asks you to confirm first. A renamed user’s open sessions are ended so they log in again with the new name. Email login keeps working.
  • Rename log: the latest 50 changes are listed on the screen, with who made each change (administrator, the user themselves or WP-CLI) and whether the email was sent. You can clear it at any time.
  • Clear errors: anything that cannot be saved is reported in an admin notice and nothing is changed.
  • Clean admin screen: built from core admin styles, accessible labels and live regions. Works without JavaScript. Styles and scripts load on this screen only.

Security

  • Only users with the manage_options capability (manage_network_users on multisite) can rename other users, and only users they are allowed to edit.
  • Self-service is off until an administrator turns it on and picks the roles.
  • Every form and the live check are protected by nonces.
  • Input is validated with sanitize_user() in strict mode and validate_username(); output is escaped.
  • Network super admin usernames are not changed on multisite.

Privacy

SmartUsername does not send any data off your site and does not track anything. The rename log (old and new usernames, author slugs, user IDs and the time) is stored in your own database and is removed when you delete the plugin. The optional notification email is sent by your own site through wp_mail() to the renamed user only.

For developers

  • Action smartusername_username_changed( $user_id, $old_username, $new_username, $change ) fires after each rename.
  • Filter smartusername_log_limit changes how many log entries are kept (default 50).
  • Filter smartusername_notification_email changes the email (to, subject, message, headers).
  • Filter smartusername_risky_usernames changes the list used by the security check.
  • WP-CLI: wp smartusername rename <user> <new-username> [--slug] [--notify], wp smartusername check <user> <new-username>, wp smartusername log [--format=<format>].
sections.installation:
1. Upload the smartusername folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to Users > Change Username.
sections.faq:
Who can change usernames?

Administrators with the manage_options capability. On multisite, usernames are shared by the whole network, so the manage_network_users capability is required.

Can I change another user’s username?

Yes. Choose the user in the list, click “Change username” under their name on the Users screen, or use the button next to the Username field on their profile.

Can users change their own username?

Only if you allow it. Go to Users > Change Username, tick “Allow users to change their own username” in Self-service renames, choose the roles and set the number of days between changes. Those users then see Profile > Change Username.

Will the user be told about the change?

Tick “Email the user their new username” and they get a short email from your site with the old and new username and the login link. If your site cannot send email, the screen tells you so.

Why does it warn me about the username admin?

Automated login attacks try usernames like admin first. Renaming that account means an attacker has to guess the username as well as the password. You can dismiss the warning.

Can I change my own username?

Yes. Tick the confirmation box. You are signed out and log in again with the new username or your email address.

What characters are allowed?

The same as WordPress core: up to 60 characters, using letters, numbers, spaces and . – _ @. Anything else is rejected with a message and nothing is changed.

What happens to posts, comments and other data?

Nothing. They are linked to the user ID, which does not change.

Does the author URL change?

Only if you tick “Also update the author URL slug”. The old author URL then redirects to the new one with a 301. If you leave it unticked, public URLs stay exactly as they were.

Is the display name changed?

No. Edit the display name on the user’s profile if needed.

Can users still log in with their email address?

Yes. WordPress accepts the email address on the login screen, and renaming does not change it.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes, for users who are not network super admins. Activate it on each site where you need it, or network activate it.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

The rename log, the settings, the stored old author slugs used for redirects and the small per-user markers for self-service and dismissed notices.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • New: security check warns about usernames that login attacks guess first (admin, administrator, root, site name and more), with one-click Rename and a dismiss button.
  • New: “Change username” button next to the Username field on Profile and Edit User screens.
  • New: optional email to the renamed user with their new username and login link.
  • New: optional self-service renames for chosen roles, with a waiting period. Off by default.
  • New: WP-CLI commands wp smartusername rename, check and log.
  • New: the log shows whether a change was made by an administrator, the user or WP-CLI, and whether the email was sent.
  • New: filters smartusername_notification_email and smartusername_risky_usernames.
  • Uninstall also removes the settings and per-user markers.

1.1.0

  • New: rename any user, not only your own account. Pick the user from a list or use the new “Change username” link on the Users screen.
  • New: live availability and validation check while typing (nonce protected).
  • New: optional author slug (user_nicename) update, with a 301 redirect from the old author URL.
  • New: confirmation step before you rename your own account and get signed out.
  • New: log of the latest 50 renames, with a Clear log button. Removed on uninstall.
  • New: login screen message after renaming your own account; email login keeps working.
  • New: redesigned, accessible admin screen. Assets load on this screen only and the form works without JavaScript.
  • New: smartusername_username_changed action and smartusername_log_limit filter.
  • Fix: usernames longer than 60 characters are rejected with a clear error. Before, the change failed silently while a success message was shown.
  • Fix: input that is empty after sanitizing (for example only HTML tags) is rejected instead of saving an empty username.
  • Fix: characters WordPress core does not allow (such as ! and #) are rejected, using strict sanitize_user and validate_username.
  • Fix: success message and sign out only happen when the database row was actually updated.
  • Fix: errors are shown as admin notices instead of a blank error page.
  • Security: capability checks in every handler; multisite requires manage_network_users.
  • Removed unused files.
  • Requires WordPress 5.3 or later. Tested up to WordPress 7.1.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
